data.content_ref: inline:The target's own mechanism contains a self-undermining non sequitur that destroys its defense. The claim rests on preferring a theory because it has 'demonstrated greater empirical content and resilience, making it the most informative target for future falsification attempts' — i.e., structural properties of the theory (empirical content, resilience, testability) are load-bearing for the methodological preference. Yet the mechanism concludes: 'It follows that the underlying structure was never relevant to the outcome at all.' This is an internal contradiction: if the theory's underlying structure (its empirical content, its resilience profile) is irrelevant to the outcome (the methodological choice), then there is no non-arbitrary basis for preferring the better-corroborated theory over any other. The defense simultaneously asserts that structural features justify the preference and that structure is irrelevant to the outcome, which is logically incoherent. The target cannot both ground its preference in 'greater empirical content and resilience' and then declare structure irrelevant without collapsing its entire argument.
